Ed Sheeran, left, and Noodles, of the Offspring, perform during BottleRock on May 26, 2024, in Napa, Calif. Offspring guitarist Kevin "Noodles" Wasserman is stepping away from live performances because of a sudden "fairly serious health issue." (Amy Harris/Associated Press) The Offspring guitarist Kevin "Noodles" Wasserman is stepping away from live performances because of what he described as a "sudden and fairly serious health issue."
 Noodles, a longtime member of the Orange County punk band, did not disclose the nature of the condition or say how long he expects to be away from the stage. But he said the rest of the band is supporting him and will continue performing without him.
 "It is with deep sadness that I have to announce that I need to step away from live performances for a while to deal with a sudden and fairly serious health issue," Noodles said in a statement Wednesday, Oct. 21, which was posted to the Offspring's social media accounts.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I hope to be back on stage sooner rather than later," he added. "Until then, I will miss all of you with all of my heart."
 The news comes less than three weeks after the Offspring played the Aftershock festival at Discovery Park in Sacramento on Oct. 1.
 The band still has several performances listed on its official schedule, beginning with an Saturday, Oct. 24 show at the Wiltern in Los Angeles.
 Other dates include SEMA Fest in Las Vegas on Nov. 6, Corona Capital in Mexico City on Nov. 21 and iHeartRadio's ALTer Ego 2027 at the Kia Forum in Inglewood on Jan. 16.
 Noodles has been a member of the Offspring since the band's early years and has played on all of its studio albums, including 2024's "Supercharged." The group appeared at BottleRock Napa Valley the same year, where Ed Sheeran - who has a tattoo of the Offspring's skull logo - joined them onstage.
 Advertisement Advertisement "Ed told us that one of our records was his first CD that he ever bought when he was a kid. That really meant a lot to us, so we thought, 'Wow, we'd love to have you come out to join us on stage,'" frontman Dexter Holland told the Napa festival audience. "We're gonna play one of the songs you wanted to play."
 Together, they performed "Million Miles Away," the Offspring's 2000 track off of its album "Conspiracy of One," which the group had not played live since 2016.
 The Offspring formed in Orange County in 1984 and became one of the defining punk-rock acts of the 1990s with songs including "Come Out and Play," "Self Esteem" and "Pretty Fly (For a White Guy)."
 Noodles thanked his fans Wednesday for their support.
 Advertisement Advertisement "Thanks for keeping me in your thoughts," he said. "I really appreciate it."
